card: Switches getblocktemplate cache age tracking to a steady clock instead of the system clock. This prevents wall-clock adjustments from causing premature or delayed block template rebuilds after mempool updates. It addresses review feedback on #36356 and updates related test harnesses where mocktime does not affect steady clock intervals. Depends on #36356 and #36921.
evidence: Description notes it was suggested during review: 'as pointed out in a review comment, a steady clock is the better fit for measuring an interval, since system time changes don't affect it'
Author references prior pattern #30372 where SteadyClock was adopted for interval measurement in RandAddSeedPerfmon
problem: When the mempool updates, getblocktemplate throttles template rebuilds by checking whether the cached template is older than 5 seconds using the system clock. Changes or jumps in system time can cause premature or delayed template rebuilds.

risk.why: A timing logic error in the template rebuild interval could cause getblocktemplate to rebuild too frequently or serve stale block templates longer than expected to miners.

scope_notes: Only the final commit is new; the preceding four commits are inherited from dependencies #36356 and #36921.
summary: Switches the getblocktemplate cache age measurement from the system clock to a steady clock. This prevents system clock adjustments from skewing the 5-second rebuild interval after mempool changes. The PR also updates unit and functional tests to accommodate steady clock behavior since mocktime no longer advances it.
